results.content: In this work, we aimed to approach differences in the emotions perceived by viewers when watching audiovisual projects produced with pastel colors compared with those produced with saturated colors. This research brings more knowledge to how pastel color in images, particularly those of an audiovisual nature, can be used to evoke emotions in the audience. results.title: Pastel color does not modulate viewers' emotions in audiovisual ...
results.content: To study this, we created 12 videos, six with a saturated color production design and six with a pastel color production design, evoking six basic emotions: disgust, anger, fear, happiness, sadness, and surprise. We analyzed the intensity of each of the studied emotions as dependent variables across both conditions (saturated and pastel videos) to address our research question: how does pastel color in audiovisuals modulate viewers’ emotional responses? The aim of this work was to study the impact that pastel colors could have on viewers’ emotions, compared to saturated colors. When looking at the data in detail, our findings revealed significant differences in only 4 out of the 36 comparisons made (11.11%), specifically in videos representing disgust and anger, where pastel color production resulted in a less intense emotional response in only three of the cases. So, since pastel color alone in audiovisuals may not be a strong determinant of emotional response, future research could explore additional contexts in which pastel tones might influence viewers’ affective reactions —such as educational videos, branding and marketing contexts, or different narrative genres.
